elements.label: Figure 6.3: Out-of-pocket health expenditure remains high
elements.description:
Line chart. Y-axis: "Share of total health expenditure" (%), gridlines at 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%. X-axis: years 2010 to 2018. Legend: Vietnam (teal), Lower middle income (orange), Upper middle income (grey), East Asia & Pacific (yellow).

Values printed for Vietnam: 2010 37%, 2011 37%, 2012 41%, 2013 41%, 2014 42%, 2015 43%, 2016 45%, 2017 45%, 2018 45%.

Approximate readings for the other series:
- Lower middle income: ~57 (2010), ~55 (2011), ~54 (2012), ~55 (2013), ~53 (2014), ~53 (2015), ~52 (2016), ~52 (2017), ~51 (2018).
- Upper middle income: ~33 flat from 2010 to 2014, ~32 in 2015, ~33 in 2016 to 2018.
- East Asia & Pacific: ~25 (2010), ~24 (2011), ~24 (2012), ~25 (2013), ~25 (2014), ~26 (2015), ~25 (2016), ~26 (2017), ~26 (2018).

Vietnam's share rises steadily from 37% to 45% and ends above the upper middle income and East Asia & Pacific series, while lower middle income stays highest throughout but drifts down.

elements.label: Figure 6.4: Catastrophic health expenditure has been declining slightly (% of households)
elements.description:
Grouped bar chart. Y-axis: "Share of households (%)", 0 to 20. X-axis: years 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016. Legend: Urban (teal), Rural (orange).

Values printed (Urban / Rural):
- 2002: 9.9 / 13.6
- 2004: 13.7 / 16.6
- 2006: 12.4 / 15.2
- 2008: 11.6 / 15.7
- 2010: 10.0 / 12.6
- 2012: 8.8 / 9.4
- 2014: 7.5 / 10.8
- 2016: 9.9 / 9.5

Rural values are higher than urban in every year except 2016. Both series peak around 2004 to 2008 and generally decline, with a dip in 2014 for urban and a small rise in 2016 for urban.
